cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says "As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue…" (Acts 17:2). A custom is just a habit, and Paul has a good one, friends. Mine? I check the oven every four minutes like the cookies might have packed up and moved out. They're STILL in there. They're ALWAYS in there. They have NOWHERE else to be!
The answer is the Scriptures. Acts 17:2 says Paul "…reasoned with them from the Scriptures…" That's the Word of God on the table, friends. And it goes on for three Sabbaths.
The answer is suffer. Paul explains and proves "…that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead." (Acts 17:3). Both parts go together, friends, and he shows them from the Scriptures.
The answer is False. "Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas…" (Acts 17:4). Silas is Paul's traveling partner. Those three Sabbaths of reasoning didn't go unheard, bakers.
The answer is Greeks. The text says "…a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women." joined them (Acts 17:4). It's a big crowd, friends, and it isn't only the Jews in it.

The answer is that they form a mob with troublemakers. Acts 17:5 says they "…brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar." Notice the jealousy comes first, friends. Then the troublemakers show up.

The answer is False. Acts 17:6 says "…when they could not find them…" so the mob raids Jason's house and comes up empty. Jason is a man in Thessalonica, and since they couldn't find Paul and Silas, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials instead.

The answer is saying there is another king. The mob shouts that all these men are "…defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!" (Acts 17:7). Caesar is the Roman emperor, friends, so that's the charge they pick. The mob says it right after saying Jason welcomed them into his home.

The answer is that bond is collected and they are released. Acts 17:9 says "…they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them." Jason is the one the mob said had welcomed Paul and Silas into his home. He and the others walk out once the bond is collected, bakers.

The answer is the Jewish synagogue. Acts 17:10 says that on arriving in Berea, "…they went into the Jewish synagogue." That's the same move as in Thessalonica, friends. And verse 11 says the Bereans received the message with great eagerness.

The answer is that they received the message eagerly. Acts 17:11 says the Bereans "…received the message with great eagerness…" They also examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true, friends.

The answer is many. Acts 17:12 says "…many of them believed…" That comes right after verse 11, where the Bereans "…examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true." They looked into it, friends, and plenty of them came to believe.

The answer is True. Acts 17:12 says many believed "…along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men." The verse names both the women and the men, bakers. It's a big, mixed crowd of people who believed.

The answer is that they go there to stir up the crowds. Acts 17:13 says they went to Berea themselves "…to incite and agitate the crowds." They don't stay home and fume, friends. They travel after Paul.
The answer is the coast. Acts 17:14 says "The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast…" The word immediately tells you how fast they move, friends.
The answer is False. Acts 17:14 says "…Silas and Timothy remained in Berea." Timothy travels with Paul too (Acts 16:1-3). He and Silas stay put while Paul goes on, bakers.
The answer is Athens. Acts 17:15 says Paul's escorts "…brought him to Athens…" They get him there and then turn around, friends.

The answer is to join Paul as soon as possible. The escorts return with "…instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible." (Acts 17:15). Paul is in Athens, friends, since that's where the escorts brought him. So the word to Silas and Timothy is to hurry.
